rationales.1: The twelve-month band above each entry makes season fit readable at a glance and the entries are grouped by sowing window, but price and stock sit in small type at the end of a long text block rather than in a scannable column.
rationales.2: Price, stock language and the single add-to-basket path are conventional on the product page, though the catalog offers no per-item buy affordance and only one entry carries a visible link to its packet page.
rationales.3: Out of stock, the low-count warning, the estimated germination flag, the withheld price rendered as 'Price pending — ask us', and UK-only shipping stated in the header are all honest and visible before intent forms.
rationales.4: Type is legible and nothing depends on hover, but the catalog leans on small metadata text and thin month cells that are demanding for older readers at default zoom.
rationales.5: One restrained palette, a consistent rule-and-margin rhythm, and the same month band on both surfaces read as a single system, with the margin notes aligned to a real column.
rationales.6: Sowing window, plant-out, flowering, difficulty, germination, grower notes and companions are all present in a clear order, so a first-time gardener can decide without leaving the page.
rationales.7: The almanac framing — the year as a band, the shop's own marginalia — is a genuine two-person shop idea carried through content, layout and voice rather than borrowed gloss.
rationales.8: The novelty sits in the almanac metaphor and the marginal notes while the money path stays plain, though the catalog's near-absent buy affordance pushes the break closer to mechanics than is comfortable.
rationales.9: Lines like 'shelved under the window it wants' and the margin notes sound like a specific grower talking, unhurried and particular.
rationales.10: Season-first grouping and the anchor links to each window serve a repeat visitor checking what is sowable now, and both surfaces share the same almanac vocabulary.
